50889809.DESCRIPTION: Binding affinity to human G9a in presence of SAM by isothermal titration calorimetry
50889809.references_previous: Xiong Y, Li F, Babault N, et al. Discovery of potent and selective inhibitors for G9a-like protein (GLP) lysine methyltransferase. J Med Chem. 2017;60:1876–1891.

original_paragraph.ITC Measurements: Isothermal titration calorimetry (ITC) measurements were made at 25 °C on a MicroCal ITC200 Instrument (Malvern Instruments). Co-concentrated G9a-SAM and GLP-SAM (protein/SAM molar ratio of 1:5) were diluted at 35 μM in ITC buffer [50 mM Tris (pH 8.0), 150 mM NaCl] supplemented with 1% DMSO. Compound 13 and 17 were prepared in DMSO at 50 mM and diluted to 0.5 mM in ITC buffer with a final DMSO concentration of 1%. Binding constants were calculated by fitting the data using the ITC data analysis module in Origin 7.0 (OriginLab Corp.).
original_paragraph.Figure 2 caption: Fig. 2. Binding confirmation of 13 and 17. Isothermal titration calorimetry (ITC) was used to confirm that 13 displayed better binding affinity to GLP (A) over G9a (B). Similarly, 17 also preferably bound to GLP (C) over G9a (D). ITC experiments were performed in triplicate.
original_paragraph.Figure 2 data: A: N 0.92, Kd 57 ± 8 nM, ΔH -11.92 ± 0.07 kcal/mol, ΔS -6.8 cal/mol/deg; B: N 0.90, Kd 510 ± 62 nM, ΔH -9.41 ± 0.11 kcal/mol, ΔS -2.8 cal/mol/deg; C: N 0.97, Kd 94 ± 14 nM, ΔH -7.94 ± 0.05 kcal/mol, ΔS -5.5 cal/mol/deg; D: N 0.94, Kd 1070 ± 80 nM, ΔH -5.5 ± 0.05 kcal/mol, ΔS 8.8 cal/mol/deg
original_paragraph.Results section: The binding of 13 and 17 to GLP and G9a was assessed using isothermal titration calorimetry (ITC) in the presence of SAM (Fig. 2) as described previously.46 Compound 13 displayed higher binding affinity to GLP (Kd = 57 ± 8 nM) than G9a (Kd = 510 ± 62 nM). Similarly, compound 17 exhibited stronger binding affinity to GLP (Kd = 94 ± 14 nM) than G9a (Kd = 1070 ± 80 nM). Therefore, both compounds are confirmed to selectively bind to GLP over G9a in the ITC biophysical assay.
